name: Uruguay
snapshot: One of the world's most stable democracies, where centre-left Yamandú Orsi took office in 2025 in a smooth handover typical of Uruguayan politics.
culture: Uruguay is Latin America's most secular country; the state renamed Christmas "Family Day" a century ago. Mate is carried everywhere in a thermos. Candombe drumming, with African roots, fills Montevideo's streets during carnival, the longest in the world. Football heroics, including two World Cup wins, are central to national identity.
society: Uruguay has the lowest poverty and inequality in Latin America, a large middle class and one of the highest shares of renewable electricity anywhere. It was the first country to legalise cannabis, in 2013, and was early on same-sex marriage. Rising crime linked to drug trafficking is the main public worry.
situation: Yamandú Orsi of the left-wing Frente Amplio, a protégé of former president José Mujica, won the November 2024 runoff and took office in March 2025. Mujica died in May 2025. By August 2026, one pollster found 57 percent of Uruguayans disapproved of Orsi's government.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years with no immediate re- election; the General Assembly has a Senate and a Chamber of Representatives. Its parties are among the most institutionalised in Latin America.
